**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep payloads out of the streaming validator**

When importing a valid archive near the 256 MiB limit, this clones every full base64 payload into `ConversationExportValidator`, which remains alive until the final turn, while the same records are also staged in SQLite. Later validation uses only each digest's media type and byte length, so retaining almost the entire upload on the Rust heap defeats the bounded streaming design and can cause Desktop imports to run out of memory; store only the required metadata here.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L20-L22](https://github.com/vishaltandale00/relayer-graphcomplete/blob/a55e1c87ee59ec608f6c784a76462913be641788/AGENTS.md#L20-L22)

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Copy Buffer-backed file bytes before queueing**

When a `HarnessFileHandle.read()` implementation returns a Node `Buffer`—which satisfies the declared `Uint8Array` return type—`Buffer.slice()` creates an alias rather than an owning copy. A caller mutation reaction after the read resolves can therefore run before the serialized worker resumes and alter the bytes used for validation, hashing, and persistence; create a guaranteed copy such as `new Uint8Array(await read())` instead.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Version visual-content records before emitting them**

Image-bearing exports now insert a new `visualAssetContent` record while still advertising `exportVersion: 1`. The existing V1 contract in `docs/conversation-export-v1.md` defines every post-header record as a turn, requires readers to reject unknown record types, and requires a new version when required structure changes, so every such export deterministically fails in prior V1 importers despite claiming compatibility; introduce a new export version with version-specific decoding or use a genuinely backward-compatible V1 representation.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Enforce writer scope before returning accepted assets**

Any in-process client holding a public `GraphWriter` for one completion can call this method with a guessed accepted node ID from another thread or project and receive its pinned bytes and provenance, because the table query checks only `node.state='accepted'`; this also works after the writer's authority becomes stale. Match `get_node` by checking active authority and `NodeTable::visible(&self.scope, node_id)` in the same transaction, while keeping the deliberately trusted unscoped `GraphDatabase` method separate.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bound generic resolve IDs before concurrent lookup**

The generic graph visual-assets route permits `resolve`, but this path accepts an arbitrary string array and immediately creates one asynchronous multi-scope lookup per entry. A capability holder can therefore submit a request within the 12 MiB body limit containing hundreds of thousands of duplicate or empty IDs, forcing a very large `Promise.all` allocation while the graph server retains the completion's asset-generation gate; apply the dedicated resolver's 32-ID, uniqueness, and identity bounds before forwarding or remove `resolve` from the generic route.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Resolve context assets from their presenting layer**

When a visual node is attached as composer context, the user navigates to another layer, and then reopens that node through the context preview's “Open details” control, `selectedContextTarget` still records the node's presenting interaction and layer but this resolver sends the currently visible ones instead. The app-server asset route loads that current layer and rejects because it does not contain the context node, so every valid image mount degrades to unavailable; derive the product interaction corresponding to the context target's `sourceInteractionNodeId` and use its `sourceLayerId` for the asset request.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Ignore labels hidden by an ancestor**

When an authored input has a native `<label>` inside an `aria-hidden="true"` ancestor and a valid visible fallback such as `title`, the compiler excludes that label by walking its ancestors and accepts the fallback name. The DOM still exposes the structurally associated label through `element.labels`, but this traversal checks only the label's own `aria-hidden`, so review publishes the hidden text instead of the compiler-approved name and deterministic lookup by that authored name fails; apply the same ancestor-hidden check to native labels.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Verify the exact Sharp native dependency closure**

On macOS, this check passes for any versioned `sharp-<platform>-<arch>-*.node` and never requires the addon's declared `@img/sharp-libvips-<platform>-<arch>` payload. A pruned or stale package can therefore retain, for example, a 0.34 addon while the bundled Sharp 0.35.4 loader and libvips files are missing, yet afterPack reports success and the packaged runtime fails as soon as `@relayer/visual-assets` imports Sharp; require the exact locked addon filename and its target libvips payload.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
